Babur the Tightfist

Overview

Babur the Tightfist is the Gipath craftsman known from Zak’s journey. A forged message brings him into the Free Hunters’ camp. He sends Kir after a supposed magical needle to obtain lizard hides for armour, and directs his search for the Magic Orb toward Estera. Later his captivity among the orcs and transfer to an ogre make him the subject of another rescue. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

The Free Hunters and Babur

A messenger invites the rescuers of the hunters to Bor the Cunning’s camp. Bor claims neutrality in the war, yet asks them to act against the village’s hunters and caravans. To question Babur the Tightfist about the Orb, Kir helps bring him out of the village. The letter can go to Babur himself or to the elder, with different explanations for the craftsman’s arrival. Babur then sends Kir to the lizards’ tomb for a supposed magical needle. The expedition supplies lizard hides, and Babur admits that useful armour material was his real interest. For information about the Orb, he redirects the visitors to Estera. [6, 7, 8, 9, 1, 2, 5, 3]

Babur’s knife bargain and captivity

Airy’s warning about the depleted Orb leads Kir towards the observatory. Babur can open the blocked approach, but first demands the Chosen’s knife, now a sacred relic. While Kir pursues the relic, island orcs raid the hunters’ camp and carry Babur away. They hand him to their ogre neighbours after his dealings with them turn sour. Kir obtains the two keys to the pit, frees the craftsman and escorts him back alive. Babur renounces further trade with the orcs. His rescue also lets Bor put forward a new plan against the settlers. [10, 11, 4, 12, 13, 14, 15]

Babur’s rescue and the restored Orb

The stolen Orb stands on an island orc pedestal. Kir obtains the bridge gear from their gathering on Council Mountain to reach it. Once Babur is safe and has seen the damaged Orb, he provides the key to the observatory approach. The observatory book lets Estera prescribe washing the Orb in underground spring water. A landslide closes Kir’s former route to Tka-Rik, forcing him through the old tunnel. Before departure, Airy asks Kel to greet the Chosen if they meet him and says she still remembers him. Kel apologises for her earlier jealousy; both women recognise feelings Kir has yet to understand. The repaired Orb shows snow rather than Jigran. Tka-Rik interprets this as Ingos, agrees that Kel can go with Kir, and warns that greater freedom there does not prevent cruel government or make their search for powerful magic safe. [16, 10, 11, 4, 12, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 13]
